name: Write and schedule a week of LinkedIn posts in your own voice with ContentIn MCP and Slack approval

parameters.content:
## LinkedIn week in your voice with ContentIn

### How it works
Every Monday the workflow takes three short notes about your week, asks ContentIn for your voice profile and material (get_voice_context), turns each note into a brief, has ContentIn write the post in your voice (write_post_in_my_voice) and asks for a schedule preview (schedule_post). The exact text lands in Slack. Only after you click Approve does the workflow send the confirmation token back, so nothing is ever queued without you. Declined posts stay as drafts in your ContentIn account.

### Setup
1. Create a ContentIn account (free, no card) at https://app.contentin.io/signup?product=agent&ref=n8n_template and paste your LinkedIn URL. The voice profile is free; the tools need the Agent plan (29 USD per LinkedIn profile per month, 7-day trial, card required) or the web Growth plan or higher.
2. In ContentIn open Profiles, then Connections, then Connect AI clients, and create an API key (it starts with cimcp_).
3. In n8n create a Header Auth credential: Name X-MCP-Key, Value your key. Select it on every ContentIn node (MCP Client and MCP Client Tool).
4. Connect LinkedIn inside ContentIn (scheduling needs it). Add your OpenAI credential on the chat model node and a Slack credential on the Slack nodes.
5. Replace the three sample notes in Your notes and slots, or swap that node for a Google Sheets read.

### Customization
Change post_days and post_hour for your slots. Replace Slack with Gmail or Send Email (both have Send and Wait). Docs: https://contentin.io/linkedin-mcp-server/setup/ Support: support@contentin.io

## Nothing posts without you

`schedule_post` is two-step by design. The first call returns the exact text plus a one-time `confirm_token` (valid 5 minutes, bound to that text). This workflow:
1. shows you the exact text in Slack and waits for **Approve** or **Decline**;
2. after Approve, requests a fresh preview, checks the text is byte-identical to what you approved, and only then sends the token back.

If the text changed in between, nothing is scheduled and Slack tells you. Declined posts stay as drafts in ContentIn.

Fair use on agent plans: at most **3 scheduled or published posts per profile per day**. The three slots below are on three different days.

Writing caps: Agent 30 posts + 50 ideas / month, Agent Pro 100 + 200.

**Unverified when this template was written (2026-11-09):** typeVersions (AI Agent 2.2, OpenAI Chat Model 1.2, MCP Client Tool 1.2, MCP Client 1.1, Slack 2.3) were taken from published n8n templates and the n8n source on GitHub; your n8n may show a newer version. If a node imports with a warning, open it and re-select the same settings. Slack **Send and wait for approval** needs a public n8n URL (n8n Cloud or a reachable webhook URL).

assignments.name: note_1
assignments.value: Last week a client asked me to cut our onboarding from 14 days to 5. We did it by removing two approval steps nobody could explain. Their first invoice went out on day 6.

assignments.name: note_2
assignments.value: I still think most founders post about the wrong thing: lessons they read, not things they did. My own posts about actual client work get three times the replies.

assignments.name: note_3
assignments.value: Numbers from October: 11 discovery calls, 4 proposals, 2 signed. Both wins came from people who had commented on my posts before, not from cold outreach.

nodes.name: Your notes and slots
nodes.notes: Replace the three notes with yours, or swap this node for Google Sheets (one row = one note). utc_offset = your LinkedIn audience's offset. post_days: 1=Mon … 7=Sun.

options.systemMessage: You turn one rough note from a founder into a brief for ContentIn's write_post_in_my_voice tool. Step 1: call get_voice_context with topic = a one-sentence summary of the note. Step 2: read voice.writing_guide, rules, strategy and the material it returns. Step 3: answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else: {"user_idea": string, "style": "authority"|"proof"|"growth", "user_constraints": string}. user_idea must keep the note's own words, numbers and names verbatim and may add only facts that appear in the returned material (cite none you did not see). Never invent details. style: results or client wins = proof, educational or frameworks = authority, broad resonance = growth. user_constraints: the user's rules from get_voice_context that matter for this post (language, no hashtags, length), in one sentence.
